name: A01: Broken Access Control
evidence: Authenticated resource-scoped routes with identifier parameters exist, including /api/Users/:id, /api/Cards/:id, /api/Addresss/:id, and /rest/basket/:id.

name: A02: Cryptographic Failures
evidence: The application includes JWT authentication, login and password-reset flows, password handling, 2FA, encryption-key serving, and cryptographic/Web3 functionality.

name: A03: Injection
evidence: The architecture reports Sequelize ORM usage, no raw SQL queries, no MongoDB detection, and no explicit eval/exec or query-string interpolation.

name: A04: Insecure Design
evidence: The extensive unauthenticated API surface and sensitive business flows suggest possible design weaknesses, but insecure design cannot be established reliably from route and dependency metadata alone.

name: A05: Security Misconfiguration
evidence: The application has XML parsing, CORS, Helmet, public file indexes, exposed metrics, and many undocumented routes, but parser entity settings, CORS policy, and effective security headers are not fully specified.

name: A06: Vulnerable and Outdated Components
evidence: The application has 117 dependencies, including security-sensitive packages such as express-jwt, jsonwebtoken, multer, js-yaml, libxml2-wasm, and Sequelize.

name: A07: Identification and Authentication Failures
evidence: Login, password change/reset, security-question, JWT authorization, 2FA, and rate-limited authentication-related endpoints are present.

name: A08: Software and Data Integrity Failures
evidence: The application processes uploaded YAML, XML, ZIP, and image files and includes webhook handling, creating deserialization and integrity-sensitive processing paths.

name: A09: Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
evidence: A logging module is present, along with upload metrics middleware and a publicly exposed /metrics endpoint.

name: A10: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
evidence: The /profile/image/url endpoint provides a URL-based image upload path, indicating server-side retrieval of externally supplied URLs.

name: API1: Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA)
evidence: The REST/API surface contains authenticated object routes with client-controlled identifiers, including users, cards, addresses, baskets, and feedback.

name: API2: Broken Authentication
evidence: The API exposes login, password reset, password change, JWT authorization, security-question, and 2FA flows.

name: API3: Broken Object Property Level Authorization
evidence: Broad auto-CRUD endpoints expose numerous model properties; only password and totpSecret are excluded from User routes, and most other models have no excluded attributes.

name: API4: Unrestricted Resource Consumption
evidence: The API includes file uploads, pagination-heavy auto-CRUD endpoints, search, CAPTCHA, chat, Web3 operations, and many routes without visible rate limiting.

name: API5: Broken Function Level Authorization
evidence: The API exposes administrative, accounting, product, user, challenge, wallet, and order functions with varied authorization middleware and several publicly registered sensitive-looking routes.

name: API6: Unrestricted Access to Sensitive Business Flows
evidence: Sensitive flows include registration, password reset, checkout, coupon application, wallet funding, deluxe membership, order tracking, and Web3 operations.

name: API7: Server Side Request Forgery
evidence: The profile image URL upload route indicates a server-side URL-fetching capability controlled by request input.

name: API8: Security Misconfiguration
evidence: The API has extensive undocumented coverage, public file indexes and metrics, multiple unauthenticated routes, and varied security middleware configuration.

name: API9: Improper Inventory Management
evidence: Swagger documents only one path while 109 hand-written routes and 28 auto-CRUD routes remain undocumented.

name: API10: Unsafe Consumption of APIs
evidence: The application integrates AI/OpenAI-compatible services, Web3 functionality, outbound URL-based image retrieval, and other external-resource capabilities.

name: LLM01: Prompt Injection
evidence: A chatbot uses an LLM with tool calling, so user-controlled conversational input can influence model behavior and tool selection.

name: LLM02: Sensitive Information Disclosure
evidence: LLM tools perform real database queries, including order and product/review retrieval, creating a model-mediated path to potentially sensitive application data.

name: LLM03: Supply Chain
evidence: The LLM integration depends on third-party AI SDKs and an OpenAI-compatible provider package.

name: LLM05: Improper Output Handling
evidence: The application uses Angular HTML escape hatches, but the architecture does not clearly establish whether chatbot-generated output reaches these sinks without safe encoding.

name: LLM06: Excessive Agency
evidence: The LLM can invoke tools that perform authenticated database queries and generate coupons, giving it real application capabilities.

name: LLM10: Unbounded Consumption
evidence: A chat endpoint exposes LLM processing and tool execution, while no dedicated rate limit or token/usage bound is shown for /rest/chat.
